channel.title: Canopticon — Drugs & public health
channel.description: Questions researched in depth, and articles written from what the research found.

item.title: Fred Hutch's HSV gene therapy in 2026: mouse and guinea-pig results, no human trial, and the antivirals arriving first
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: A gene therapy clears up to 97% of dormant herpes in mice. In the animal that relapses the way people do it clears above 30%, nobody has filed to test it in a person, and the drugs arriving first suppress the virus rather than remove it.

item.title: Opioid deaths and overdose calls in Hamilton: why the two counts moved in opposite directions
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: Hamilton's opioid deaths have fallen every year since 2021, while paramedic calls for overdoses more than doubled. The death count is measuring a drug supply that no longer exists.

item.title: The Fringe Pharmacopeia of HSV Latency Destruction: A Deep-Hunt Survey of Natural, Botanical, Fungal, and Bioactive Compounds
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: No natural compound has been shown to destroy or eradicate HSV latency in human neurons.

item.title: Novel and Underexplored Mechanisms for Disrupting and Destroying HSV Latency: A Mechanistic Research Pass
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: The single most mature "destruction" approach is AAV-delivered meganuclease gene editing, which eliminated over 90% of latent virus from mouse superior cervical ganglia (Aubert et al.

item.title: The State of HSV Gene-Therapy Development: Fred Hutch's Meganuclease Program and the Broader Herpes-Cure Pipeline
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: The Fred Hutch/Jerome-lab HSV meganuclease program remains preclinical (pre-IND) as of mid-2026 — no IND has been filed and no human trial has begun.

item.title: The Fentanyl Crisis Research Synthesis: Sharpest Evidence for a Long-Form Hamilton/Ontario Essay
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: This synthesis is organized by the four focus areas in your brief.

item.title: How We Got Here: A Field Guide to the Fentanyl Crisis in Canada and on Hamilton's Streets
item.dc:creator: Chris Telford
item.description: Hamilton in 2026 — the open wounds, the forward-leaning catatonia, the people who appear neither awake nor unconscious but suspended in some grotesque middle state — is not the same drug crisis Canada has been talking about for the last decade.
